name: AlphaEdit

paper.title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models

construction.unit: a batch of 100 factual rewrites (subject, relation, new object)
construction.kept_as: parametric: closed-form update to FFN output matrices
construction.processing: optimise a target hidden vector per fact (25 gradient steps), take the subject's FFN key, then solve a least-squares weight update projected onto the approximate null space of preserved-knowledge keys

organization.structure: the model's FFN output (down_proj) matrices of 5-6 consecutive layers (4-8 for LLaMA3)
organization.stores: edited weights; running sum KpKpᵀ of past edit keys; one fixed projection P per layer

management.operations: each batch adds its projected update to W and its keys to KpKpᵀ
management.conflicts: the update is penalised on keys of earlier edits (‖ΔP Kp‖²) and projected off the keys of preserved knowledge

retrieval.candidates: none: every forward pass uses the edited weights

use.context: no retrieved text; the edited weights produce the answer

classify.note: Parametric: edits are folded into the FFN weights, so there is no store to search; every prompt passes through the edited matrices.

stages.ingestion: Edits arrive in batches of 100 factual rewrites (subject, relation, new object); 2,000 in the main experiments.
stages.construction: For each fact a target hidden vector at the last edited layer is found by 25 gradient steps; its key is the FFN input at the subject's last token, averaged over the bare prompt and 5 generated prefixes.
stages.organization: Knowledge stays in the FFN output matrices of layers 4-8 (LLaMA3; 3-8 GPT-J; 13-17 GPT2-XL). A projection P per layer, computed once from 100,000 Wikipedia samples, points away from directions that preserved knowledge uses.
stages.update: Per layer, Δ = R K1ᵀ P (Kp Kpᵀ P + K1 K1ᵀ P + αI)⁻¹ is added to W (the residual is spread over the edited layers), then the batch's keys are added to Kp Kpᵀ so later batches avoid them.
stages.answer: The model answers from its edited weights in an ordinary forward pass.

summary: Locate-then-edit with one extra projection: each MEMIT-style weight update is projected onto the approximate null space of preserved-knowledge keys, so thousands of sequential edits barely move the model's other outputs.
notes: VENUE: ICLR 2025 main conference, oral (OpenReview forum HvSytvg3Jh, venue 'ICLR 2025 Oral'; the PDF header reads 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025'). CODE: github.com/jianghoucheng/AlphaEdit pinned to aac456de (2025-04-22), the last code change, same day as arXiv v4; later commits touch only README and LICENSE. This is a model-editing paper: the memory is the model's own weights, so there is no retrieval stage and the Map placement is 'none / reads everything'. TAGS: write_time=learned because the target vectors are found by gradient steps before the closed-form write; learning=training-free because no editor network or policy is trained. Main results also include memory-based editors (SERAC, GRACE, MELO) in App. C.5 Table 2, and Gemma / phi-1.5 in Table 3 (not transcribed). KnowEdit, MQuAKE and LEME results (Tables 4-5) are appendix extras, not transcribed.

sources.code_note: Official repository named in the paper. Commit aac456de (2025-04-22) is the last code change and matches arXiv v4 (2025-04-22); the repo builds on the MEMIT codebase (rome/, memit/ folders).

headline: The memory is the model's own FFN weights; nothing is stored beside them except key statistics used for later writes.
The only change from sequential MEMIT is where the update may point: into directions that preserved-knowledge keys (almost) never use.
The null space is approximate (eigenvalues below a threshold), so preserved facts still move: Counterfact specificity 89.48 → 67.88 on LLaMA3 after 2,000 edits.

units.name: Edited FFN weights
units.role: the FFN output matrices that hold both pretrained and edited facts

fields.name: W_out (layers 4-8)
fields.what: down_proj matrices of LLaMA3 (5 layers); GPT-J 3-8, GPT2-XL 13-17

fields.name: projection P
fields.what: one d0 × d0 matrix per layer, from the eigenvectors of K0K0ᵀ with small eigenvalues
fields.src: code evaluate.py L426-L443 (used only while writing)

fields.name: KpKpᵀ
fields.what: running sum of the keys of every past edit
fields.src: code AlphaEdit_main.py L146-L148 (used only while writing)

fields.name: K0K0ᵀ
fields.what: second moment of FFN keys over 100,000 Wikipedia samples; only feeds P

write.how: collect K0K0ᵀ, the key second moment at each edited layer, over Wikipedia text
SVD of K0K0ᵀ; keep eigenvectors whose eigenvalue is below the threshold; P = ÛÛᵀ; computed once before editing
write.src: paper Eq. 8-9; code evaluate.py L206-L209, L426-L443

write.how: per fact, optimise a change to the hidden state at the last edited layer so the model outputs the new object (NLL + KL + decay terms)
write.src: paper App. A.3, B.1 Eq. 24; code compute_z.py

write.how: FFN input at the subject's last token, averaged over the bare prompt and 5 generated prefixes
per layer, solve (P(K1K1ᵀ + KpKpᵀ) + αI) Δᵀ = P K1 Rᵀ; the residual R is split over the remaining edited layers
write.out: one update per layer, added to W

write.how: recompute the batch's keys on the updated model and add them to KpKpᵀ

read.how: no retrieval: the prompt runs through the edited model and each edited FFN computes (W + ΔP)k
for keys of preserved knowledge ΔP k0 ≈ 0, so their values (and answers) stay approximately the same
for an edited subject's key the new matrix yields the optimised value v*, which leads to the new object

answer_context.format: no memory text; edits act inside the FFN layers

compression.basis: Not reported. Edits add no parameters; P and KpKpᵀ are d0 × d0 matrices per edited layer used only when writing.

paper_vs_code.code: keep eigenvectors with singular value below 2e-2 (all released configs)

paper_vs_code.paper: + I in Eq. 14 (αI with α > 0 in App. B.5)
App. A.3 sets λ = 15,000 (GPT-J, LLaMA3) and 20,000 (GPT2-XL)
paper_vs_code.code: mom2_update_weight is in the configs but AlphaEdit's update never reads it (only MEMIT's does)

open_questions: How many directions P keeps per layer is not reported, so how much room the edits have, and how far from an exact null space it is, is unknown.
AlphaEdit changes three things relative to MEMIT (projection, dropping the K0 term, the ‖ΔP‖² term); Fig. 6 adds the projection to baselines, but no run separates the three.
P is computed once on the unedited model; edits to earlier layers change the keys later layers see, and the effect of not recomputing P is not studied.

glance.a: A batch of 100 facts folded into the FFN output matrices of 5 layers; there is no separate item.
No. Only weights change; the code also keeps the sum of past edit keys (KpKpᵀ) to protect them in later batches.
It is not: facts live in the weights. A fixed projection per layer limits where updates may point.

glance.q: Is memory reconstructed at question time?
glance.a: No. The edited model is queried like any model.

rows: AlphaEdit, K0 from the full sample
ablation.src: paper Table 6 (App. C.8) and Table 1; LLaMA3, 2,000 edits in batches of 100. The MEMIT row differs from AlphaEdit in more than the projection.

discussion.takeaway: Project each locate-then-edit update onto the approximate null space of preserved-knowledge keys. In its experiments this single change lets 2,000 sequential edits land without collapsing the model, and it improves MEMIT-style editors by large margins.

claims.claim: Sequential locate-then-edit degrades because each update disturbs preserved key-value pairs and shifts hidden representations.
claims.evidence: Fig. 1, Fig. 5 (t-SNE of hidden states before and after 2,000 edits), §1.

claims.claim: Best editing results across three LLMs.
claims.evidence: Table 1, LLaMA3: Counterfact Eff./Gen. 98.90/94.22 vs 83.33/67.79 for the best baseline (FT); ZsRE Eff. 94.47 vs 86.05 (RECT). Average +12.54% Eff. and +16.78% Gen. over the best baseline (§4.2).
GLUE-style F1 on SST, MRPC, CoLA, RTE, MMLU, NLI stays near the unedited level up to 3,000 edits while baselines fall toward zero after 2,000. Fig. 4, §4.3.

claims.claim: The projection is a plug-in for other editors.
claims.evidence: Adding it to MEMIT, PRUNE and RECT improves them by 28.24% (editing) and 42.65% (general capability) on average. Fig. 6-7, §4.5.

claims.claim: Better than memory-based editors on efficacy and generalization.
claims.evidence: LLaMA3 ZsRE Gen. 91.13 vs GRACE 1.03, SERAC 33.96, MELO 24.14; GRACE keeps higher Counterfact specificity (72.23 vs 67.88). Table 2, App. C.5.
231.40 s vs 231.32 s per 100 ZsRE edits on LLaMA3. Table 7.

limits: Not tested on multimodal LLMs or large reasoning models.
Applying null-space projection to other capabilities (safety, math, biochemistry) is left open.
reading: The null space is approximate, so preserved facts still move: Counterfact specificity drops from 89.48 (unedited) to 67.88 on LLaMA3 after 2,000 edits (Table 1).
P is computed once from the unedited model and not recomputed as edits to layers 4-7 change the keys that later layers see (evaluate.py L206-L209).
App. A.3 lists λ = 15,000 / 20,000, but the AlphaEdit update never reads that setting; preserved knowledge enters only through P (AlphaEdit_main.py L130-L132).
The released configs use a 2e-2 eigenvalue threshold, while the paper's footnote says 1e-2.
The same full-data LLaMA3 numbers carry ±0.10 in Table 1 and ±1.21 in Table 6, so the spreads come from different runs or calculations.
PRUNE has no public code and was reimplemented from its paper (App. A.4); ZsRE efficacy is token-level top-1 accuracy, and the unedited LLaMA3 already scores 36.99.

abstract.text: AlphaEdit addresses sequential knowledge editing, where many factual updates are written into an LLM's FFN weights one batch after another. Locate-then-edit methods such as MEMIT balance fitting the new facts against keeping old ones, and over many edits the balance fails and the model forgets or collapses. AlphaEdit instead projects each weight update onto the null space of the keys of preserved knowledge, so the fit to new facts no longer competes with preservation. With one extra line of code over MEMIT it reports large gains on Counterfact and ZsRE for LLaMA3, GPT-J and GPT2-XL, and the projection also lifts other editors.
